Chapter Eleven: The Ongoing Journey—Returning to the Crossroads
You know, even after years of following your “Must,” that old crossroads never really disappears. Life keeps moving, things change, and suddenly, you find yourself standing at that familiar intersection all over again. Sometimes, the voice of “Should” gets louder. Maybe the call of “Must” feels a little faded in the background.
It’s not a one-time thing. This journey—it’s something you come back to, again and again. Every time life shifts, you’re invited back to that moment of choice.
Picture someone who’s built their whole world around their passion. Years go by, and now, they’re pulled in new directions—work, family, maybe caring for aging parents. Suddenly, those old obligations creep back in, and “Should” tries to take the wheel again. The tug-of-war feels all too familiar, doesn’t it?
What you start to realize is, this whole journey is cyclical. There are seasons where you feel bold and expansive, ready to chase your dreams. Then there are quieter times, maybe even confusing ones, when you’re just trying to hold it all together. And that’s okay. The secret isn’t to avoid these crossroads—it’s to welcome them. Every return is a chance to grow, reflect, and renew your sense of purpose.
Most folks don’t realize that choosing “Must” isn’t something you finish. There’s always another layer, a new challenge, or a fresh opportunity to go deeper. It’s not about reaching some final destination. It’s about learning how to walk this path with courage, a little grace, and plenty of self-compassion.
One person described it perfectly—as a dance. You’re always moving between obligation and desire, responsibility and passion. The dance doesn’t have to be perfect. In fact, sometimes it’s downright messy. But it’s always real, and that’s what matters.
What makes the journey meaningful is your willingness to keep showing up. To keep choosing, keep listening, and keep honoring what’s true for you—even when it’s hard. That’s what turns the ongoing journey into something truly beautiful.
